headline: Two-step story: 2000 → 2400 (S2 + decode-2D geometry, NO training) → 2634.58 (trained general DSpark draft replacing MTP-assistant, true S2 @8192). Draft ckpt at shares/users/zxy/autobench/data/dspark_b16 (msn-dni-c09). Active: 3000 via int5/int4 W4A16 (quality-gated).

campaigns.name: Step 2 — trained general DSpark b16 draft vs S2 MTP-assistant (draft-only swap; WITH training)
campaigns.notes: Step 2 is WITH-training: a general-purpose DSpark model is trained as a speculative draft and deployed on Gemma 4 in place of the bundled Google MTP-assistant k5 (draft-only; target text_only untouched). Matched 768 (apples-to-apples): DSpark b16 (1866.46 TPS / QPS 2.98) beats S2 MTP-assistant k5 (1798.22 TPS / QPS 2.87) by +3.8% in both TPS and QPS. True-S2 DSpark @8192 decoded ~2295 tok/req at 2634.58 TPS / QPS 1.15 in 871s — closes 2000->2600. LENGTH-MISMATCH CAVEAT: MTP @8192 control decoded only ~1323 tok/req (2434.38 / 1.84) vs DSpark ~2291 — NOT apples-to-apples despite shared output_len=8192; fractional true-8192 gain over MTP remains UNPROVEN until a length-matched (>=2295 tok/req) MTP control lands. 3000 is the active target (lever matrix: int5 L1 in-flight, int4 L2, draft-accept L3, parallelism L4, fused-MoE L5).

campaigns.notes: This is the weight-precision gate (L1) on the road to 3000. Acceptance = candidate within noise of control (<1-2% abs / 1-2 sigma per benchmark on agentic tool-loop + GSM8K + BBH). int5 W4A16 ~0.63 bytes/weight vs 1.0 FP8 (~37% less weight HBM); int4 W4A16 (0.5, ~50%) follows via the same gate. Both arms were resubmitted to fresh nodes after repeated preemption (10-25); currently RUNNING. No verdict yet — results still landing.
